transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith, my name is Cathy and I'm a software developer. I'm here because in longer work meetings I just can’t stay in my seat—I keep getting up to move around even when I know it looks unprofessional.
Did you experience similar difficulties with sitting still, staying focused, or feeling restless during your childhood, or is this a relatively new development?

This definitely isn't new; it actually goes all the way back to my childhood. Even in elementary school, my teachers were always complaining to my parents that I couldn't stay in my seat, blurted out answers, and was constantly walking around the classroom when I was supposed to be working quietly.
Beyond the physical restlessness, do you frequently find yourself struggling to stay focused on tasks, making careless mistakes, or feeling like your mind wanders during these meetings?

Yes, absolutely. On Zoom calls, my mind drifts off to other projects or what I'm making for dinner after just ten minutes, and I'll realize I missed key decisions. I also get easily sidetracked, like completing a code review but completely forgetting to update the Jira ticket unless someone reminds me.
Do you often feel like you have trouble organizing your daily tasks, such as losing essential items or struggling to follow through on multi-step instructions until they are finished?

Yes, organizing is a huge struggle—when I try to plan my week, all my tasks just blur together and I bounce between them until they become urgent. I definitely get sidetracked mid-way through multi-step tasks, like completing a code review but forgetting to update the Jira ticket, though I don't really have an issue with losing physical items.

Beyond the physical restlessness and inattention, do you often find yourself acting impulsively, such as interrupting others during conversations or making quick decisions without considering the consequences?

Yes, I definitely struggle with that, especially during conversations. In one-on-one meetings with my engineers, I often jump in with solutions or finish their sentences before they've even finished explaining the problem. My brain just races ahead and I feel this strong urge to say it right away.
